directAnswer: Clear the download cache in Steam settings and restart the application. If the issue persists, verify your internet connection and ensure Steam is allowed through your firewall.
summary: To fix a Steam download stuck at 0%, clear the download cache, check your internet connection, and adjust firewall settings to ensure Steam is not blocked.

sections.heading: Clear Download Cache
sections.body: Clearing the download cache can resolve issues with stuck downloads. This is done through Steam's settings menu.

sections.heading: Check Internet Connection
sections.body: Verify that your internet connection is stable. Restart your router if necessary to refresh the connection.

sections.heading: Adjust Firewall Settings
sections.body: Ensure that Steam is not being blocked by your firewall. Add Steam as an exception in your firewall settings.

steps.title: Open Steam Settings
steps.detail: Launch Steam, click on 'Steam' in the top-left corner, and select 'Settings'.

steps.title: Clear Download Cache
steps.detail: In 'Settings', go to 'Downloads' and click 'Clear Download Cache'. Confirm the action to proceed.

steps.title: Restart Steam
steps.detail: After clearing the cache, restart Steam to apply the changes.

steps.title: Check Internet Connection
steps.detail: Ensure your internet connection is active and stable. Restart your router if needed.

steps.title: Configure Firewall
steps.detail: Access your firewall settings and add Steam as an exception to ensure it is not blocked. On Windows, go to 'Control Panel' > 'System and Security' > 'Windows Defender Firewall' > 'Allow an app or feature through Windows Defender Firewall'.

faqs.question: Why is my Steam download stuck at 0%?
faqs.answer: This can occur due to a corrupted download cache, poor internet connection, or firewall restrictions.

faqs.question: How do I clear the download cache in Steam?
faqs.answer: Go to 'Steam' > 'Settings' > 'Downloads' and click 'Clear Download Cache'.

faqs.question: What should I do if clearing the cache doesn't work?
faqs.answer: Check your internet connection, restart your router, and ensure Steam is not blocked by a firewall.

caveats: Clearing the download cache will log you out of Steam.
Firewall settings may vary depending on the software used.
Internet issues can be caused by external factors beyond your control.
